svg.title: One key, four threads: what the GIL actually costs
svg.desc: Blank version of the sketch “One key, four threads: what the GIL actually costs” with all labels removed, for drawing from memory. Four thread boxes reaching for a single hachured key labelled GIL, with only one holding it. Beside them, one core interleaving jobs A B C D versus four cores running A, B, C and D genuinely at once. Below, a two-by-four grid of measured results shows threads making a CPU-bound workload 0.86 times as fast, circled in red, while asyncio makes an I/O-bound workload 27.02 times faster, circled in green. An Amdahl curve shows 95% parallel code flattening at about 16.8x even on a hundred cores.
